newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arafat says will declare state in two years.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says will declare state in two years.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said in a radio interview broadcast in France on Friday that he would declare a Palestinian state in two years' time.
Asked by Europe-1 when a Palestinian state would exist, Arafat replied: "As soon as the interim period is over, we shall declare our Palestinian state. In two years' time."

A five-year interim period during which Israel and the Palestinians were to seek to reach a final settlement to their decades-old dispute began when Arafat signed a peace agreement with the late Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Rabin in Washington in September 1993.
But hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, elected in May, is committed to preventing the emergence of a Palestinian state.

He has expressed a preference for the autonomous areas of the West Bank and Gaza Strip to have a status vis-a-vis Israel akin to the ties between the United States and its Caribbean commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
Arafat gave the interview before leaving France on Thursday after attending a World Bank donors' meeting devoted to the Palestinian economy on Wednesday.
